title: Playing with violinists: Robichaux and others
summary: He did not care for violin because violinists were bosses; he rates Dominguez and Bocage and calls Robichaux a businessman.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Fiddlers and reading violinists of New Orleans

blocks.x: How do you like playing the clarinet with the violin? I would like it. Does the violin and clarinet work together good usually or are they about the same?
Oh yeah, I used to play with the other violin player too, John Robichaux. Oh yeah, John Robichaux. Oh yeah.
Did you like to play with the violin?

I didn't care about violin. Well? I don't like playing. I didn't care too much about violin. But they were the boss all the time. A lot of the violin players used to be leaders. They were leaders. They used to run the outfit. They run the outfit. Like Eugene Deeson. No, not Eugene Deeson. Paul Dominguez, he was a good violin player. He was a good violin player. Peter Bocard was a good violin player. And there's other fellow, I can't tell his name. Ted Dominguez? Ted Dominguez, he was a good violin player. Robichaux, he was not a good violin player. No. He was a businessman. He was a real businessman. He was a real businessman. He was a real businessman.
How about a horse? Did you ever see a horse with his violin?

I don't know. I don't know. I don't know him about his violin players. He used to play piano all the time. I know. He used to play piano all the time. But he used to play a little violin though. He used to play a little bit of all the instruments.
